# v1.4.11 - a faster cold start and a more compact carousel

- Improved: Home opens noticeably faster from a cold start. The app now warms the
  right data before you arrive, and the Trending and Newest rows are loaded first
  instead of every row starting at once, so the top of Home fills in sooner.
- Improved: the update check no longer holds up the screen. It runs in the
  background, so a slow or offline check never delays the first content you see.
- Improved: rows now appear as soon as their data is ready. If a source is slow
  to answer, Home shows what has already arrived and fills in the rest, instead
  of waiting for the slowest source before showing anything.
- Improved: carousels are more compact - cards are a little smaller with tighter
  spacing, so more titles fit across each row (about three per row on the
  compact theme and four on the default, up from two and three).
- Fixed: a Home row no longer comes up empty when a source has changed its name;
  the app falls back to showing the titles it received.
- Fixed: a stalled response from a source no longer freezes the Trending row; the
  app gives up after a short wait and moves on.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.10 - new Home rails, a faster app, and a glassier interface

- New: five more rows on Home - Top Rated, Newest Releases, Completed Series,
  Action, and Romance - each with its own View All page. Home is also airier,
  with more breathing room between sections and titles.
- Improved: switching between tabs is now instant. Tapping a tab no longer
  re-draws the whole screen or re-fetches data that has not changed, so the
  bottom bar and content stay smooth instead of stuttering on every switch.
- Improved: the app now uses the iOS 26 "Liquid Glass" look - frosted,
  rounded cards and bars, softer card shadows, a richer Home spotlight, and
  animated panels that spring open and fade closed instead of snapping.
- Improved: the reader adds a subtle page-turn animation and light haptic
  feedback on chapter and page changes, and the bottom bar no longer covers the
  "Read Now" button on a manga's page.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.9 - backend survives interrupted streams instead of crashing

- Fixed: the app no longer loses every connection and its own backend on a long
  run. A single interrupted download or response - for example a cover image the
  phone stops mid-way - could crash the embedded backend process, after which
  every source and the app's own interface stopped responding all at once.
  Interrupted stream and socket events are now treated as harmless, so the
  backend keeps running and the next request succeeds.
- Improved: the local backend now recovers from a busy port on restart instead
  of staying down, and holds connections with proper keep-alive timeouts so a
  half-open connection cannot wedge it.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.8 - Indonesian Hits covers fit, reader restores to the panel you left

- Fixed: the Indonesian Hits row on Home no longer shows cropped or zoomed
  covers. That row's sources return cover art with different proportions, which
  the shared card style was centre-cropping; the covers are now shown in full on
  those cards.
- Fixed: the reader now reopens on the panel you left on. Leaving mid-chapter
  and coming back used to land on the last panel and then jump to the next
  chapter; the saved position is now tracked per chapter and restored to the
  correct panel, and the automatic next-chapter jump no longer fires while the
  position is being restored.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.7 - the app updates itself on launch

- Improved: the app now updates itself when it starts. When a new signed version
  is available it is downloaded and verified automatically in the background,
  without slowing down startup, and applied with a single automatic restart
  while the app is idle. If you are already using the app when the update is
  ready, it simply shows a "Restart to apply" option instead of restarting.
- Fixed: the update status now correctly reports when an update has been
  installed and is waiting for a restart. Previously it always said nothing was
  pending, even after an update was downloaded and verified.
- Note: the update is still signature-verified before it is applied, and a
  failed or interrupted update never blocks the app from starting.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.6 - novel text alignment persists and long novel text wraps

- Fixed: the Text Align setting in the novel reader now sticks. Your choice of
  Left, Center, Right or Justify is saved and restored, so it survives closing
  and reopening the reader and moving between chapters; previously it reset back
  to Left every time.
- Fixed: long unbreakable novel text no longer runs off the edge of the reader
  on narrow screens. Bare URLs, OCR runs without spaces and long CJK blocks now
  wrap to the next line instead of overflowing the left or right margin.
- Improved: the novel reader settings sheet is simpler. The Speech Engine
  selector and the neural/system voice panels were removed; the remaining
  reading controls - Speech Rate, Voice, Word Animation, Highlight Color and
  Focus Mode - are unchanged.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.5 - Indonesian Hits restored and fresher recommendations

- Fixed: the "Indonesian Hits" row on Home is no longer empty. When the
  Preferred Content Region was set to a region other than Indonesian, that row
  was filtered down to nothing; a labelled row now always shows its own sources
  regardless of the region preference.
- Fixed: recommendations no longer repeat the same titles across rows. One
  series could appear in Recommended for You, Because you read, More Genre and a
  type row at the same time; each title now appears in only one row.
- Improved: building recommendations no longer makes a duplicate provider
  request, so the Home rails load a little faster.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.4 - reading counts, clearer source names, and an honest progress line

- Fixed: reading a chapter now always counts toward Chapters Read and EXP. Some
  chapters open before their title has resolved; the app used to reject those
  saves and quietly drop them, so the counters never moved. A read with an
  unresolved title now records the chapter and its EXP, the app retries once if
  a save is refused, and any remaining failure is logged instead of hidden.
- Improved: the source list now uses one flat, consistent wording - "Provider 1"
  through "Provider 31" - instead of the old "Manga/Manhwa/Manhua Provider N"
  and "Novel Provider N" buckets, so the numbering is simple and easy to follow.
- Fixed: the reader progress line now tracks the real end of the chapter. It
  used to reach 100% partway through, while page images were still settling,
  which also put it out of step with the chapter counter; it now stays in step
  with the counter as you read to the end.
- Note: no action needed on your part - just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.3 — clearer sign-in and account creation

- Improved: signing in and creating an account are now two separate views on
  both the welcome screen and the Account tab. Each view shows only the fields
  it needs, so it is always clear whether you are signing in or registering.
- Improved: the email and password you type are kept while you switch between
  the two views, so you never have to retype them.
- Fixed: on the Account tab the Sign In and Create Account buttons no longer
  appear at the same time.
- Note: no action needed on your part — just update and enjoy.

# v1.4.2 — four new sources on a shared scraper

- New: four more reading sources join the library — Toonily (manhwa),
  MangaRead (manga), ManhuaTop (manhua) and WuxiaWorld (light novel). They
  appear alongside the sources you already browse, with the same search,
  detail and chapter-list behaviour.
- Improved: these four and ManhuaPlus now share one scraper built for the
  Madara (WP-Manga) site theme, so fixes and improvements to that markup
  benefit every one of them at once.
- Note: no action needed on your part — just update and enjoy.

# v1.3.27 — OTA update UI: progress bar, install phases, restart prompt

- New: app updates now show real byte-level download progress. The install
  streams from the server and the Updates panel (and the changelog modal) show a
  true percentage bar with the downloaded/total MB as the bundle arrives, rather
  than a static "Downloading..." label.
- New: an install phase checklist walks through Download → Verify → Install →
  Restart. The current step spins while it runs and each finished step gets a
  checkmark, so it is clear what the update is doing.
- New: an update-available banner appears in the Updates panel and at the top of
  the changelog modal, showing the new version, the download size, the release
  date and an Install action.
- New: the changelog list is polished with a version chip, a "Latest" badge on
  the newest entry, and human-friendly relative dates (today / yesterday /
  N days ago).
- New: after an update installs, a restart prompt offers "Restart Now" or
  "Later". Choosing "Later" leaves a persistent reminder in the Updates panel
  until the app is actually restarted.
- Fixed: the `hidden` helper now hides and shows the new update panels
  correctly — the OTA elements use scoped `.hidden` rules instead of a global
  rule that would have clobbered the navigation slide-out and scroll-indicator
  fades.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.22 — Mgeko source back online

- Fixed: the Mgeko source returned no results and reported a TLS/certificate
  error. The cause was not an expired certificate on Mgeko itself — it was local
  network DNS interference returning the wrong server for the Mgeko host, which
  made the secure connection fail. Mgeko's host is now resolved correctly, so
  search, popular listings, details and chapters work again, with full
  certificate validation preserved.
- Fixed: Mgeko cover images hosted on the same affected host now load again
  through the image proxy.
- Note: this is a network-resolution fix only; nothing about your library or
  reading progress changes.

# v1.3.8 — Library update badge reads "New Ch. <n>"

- Fix: the Library update badge now reads "New Ch. 45" instead of "New 45".
  In the App Store themes the Library renders inset list rows, whose badge
  omitted the "Ch." prefix; the legacy grid card already showed "New Ch.". Both
  renderers are now consistent.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.7 — History: swipe-only delete + iOS History surface

- Fix: History rows no longer show a permanent red "Remove" bar at rest. In the
  App Store themes the row body is transparent, so the red swipe layer showed
  through and tapping it opened the reader instead of deleting. The red action
  is now hidden and non-interactive until the row is actually swiped, in every
  theme — tapping a row body opens the reader, as expected.
- History delete is now swipe-only: swipe a row left (or drag with a mouse) and
  tap the revealed red action to remove the entry. The always-visible per-row
  delete button is gone.
- History (App Store themes): the search field gains an iOS Cancel button and
  live debounced filtering, the toolbar shows an item count plus a Clear action
  (with a confirmation prompt), and each day-group header shows its item count.
- History rows in the App Store themes get slightly roomier padding.
- Dark (Legacy) and Light (Legacy) keep their existing History styling.

# v1.3.3 — Performance & stability hardening

## What changed

### Server hot paths

- **Bounded caches.** The in-memory caches that backed chapter and API lookups
  now have hard size caps, so long-running sessions can no longer grow them
  without limit.
- **SQLite tuned for reads.** Added the missing indexes plus sensible pragmas
  and a prepared-statement cache, cutting repeated query overhead on the
  hot paths.
- **`/api/health` under control.** Health checks now run with bounded
  concurrency so a burst of probes can't stampede the process.
- **Crash safety.** Express error middleware catches async route failures, and
  an `uncaughtException` handler logs and exits with `process.exit(1)` instead
  of leaving the server in a broken state. Request bodies are capped at 6mb.
- **Cheaper logging.** Log writes are batched instead of flushing on every
  line.

### Downloads

- **The queue is now O(N) instead of O(N²).** Enqueue/dequeue no longer rescan
  the whole queue on every operation.
- **Real cancellation.** Cancelling a download actually stops its in-flight
  work rather than letting it finish in the background.
- **500-chapter clamp.** A single batch is clamped to 500 chapters so one
  request can't pin the queue.

### Client runtime

- **Reader scrolling is smooth.** Scroll handling is coalesced through
  `requestAnimationFrame` and layout measurements are cached.
- **No more listener leaks.** Event listeners are properly torn down when
  views are replaced.
- **API traffic deduped and bounded.** Identical in-flight requests are
  deduped, the client cache has a size cap, and retries are capped.
- **Lazy modules.** `tts.js` loads on demand.

### Startup weight & offline

- **Lighter boot.** The render-blocking Tesseract CDN script is gone, `marked`
  is deferred, and an unused OpenCV inpaint worker was dropped.
- **Safer service worker.** The dynamic cache is bounded and an offline shell
  fallback serves when the network is unavailable.

### OTA durability

- **Staging dirs are pruned and installs are serialized**, so an interrupted or
  concurrent update can't leave partial state behind.

## Notes

- No user-facing feature changes; this release is about keeping the app fast and
  stable under load and over long sessions.
- Adds 8 regression test files guarding the caches, queue limits, logger
  batching, OTA cleanup and service-worker behaviour.

# v1.2.15 — The App Store theme, everywhere

## The carousels finally look like the App Store

The App Store theme already had the right colours, fonts, and controls, but the
home carousels still used the old three-up grid. Now the whole layout follows
the App Store language.

## What changed

- **Carousel rails** — larger, edge-to-edge cards (~2.15 visible on a phone,
  with the next card peeking) instead of a cramped three-up row. The default
  dark and light themes keep their original sizing.
- **Carousel arrows** — the prev/next buttons stay visible on desktop and hide
  on touch devices, styled as frosted iOS glass circles.
- **Scroll indicator** — restyled as a thin iOS page indicator with a blue
  pill thumb, centred under each rail.
- **Section headers** — App Store large-title rhythm; the "View All" link is
  now Apple-blue text with a chevron instead of a tinted pill.
- **Featured cards** — the large "story" card gets rounded corners, an accent
  subtitle, and a pill Read button.
- **See-all tile** — a solid iOS card with a chevron instead of a dashed box.
- **Packs** — borderless cards with soft shadows, pill filter chips, and a
  rounded select field.
- **Novels** — the sub-tabs are now a proper segmented control.
- **Library** — history entries render as a grouped inset list with hairline
  separators.
- **Account** — stat tiles are iOS cards with system-font numbers.
- **States** — empty, error, search, and loading placeholders all use the
  theme's glass surfaces and shimmer tokens.

## Unchanged

Dark (still the default) and Light are untouched, and the App Store theme is
still opt-in under **Account → App Settings → UI Theme**. Your saved choice is
applied before the first paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme.

# v1.2.12 — CGBUM chapters actually load

## The bug

Opening any CGBUM chapter showed blank pages. The images never arrived, so the
reader sat on placeholders no matter how long you waited.

The cause was not, as an earlier note claimed, that the image host blocks
datacenter traffic. The real reason is that CGBUM's chapter image server
(`cdn8.cgbum.com`) refuses every request that does not carry a special
`cgbum_reader_ts` cookie, which the chapter page itself hands out when it
loads. That cookie is marked HttpOnly, so the app's WebView cannot read it, and
it also expects a `cgbum.com` referer. The backend captured neither, so every
image came back rejected and the reader had nothing to show.

## The fix

- **The backend now keeps the cookie.** When it fetches a chapter page it reads
  the cookie the page sets and attaches it to each image in that chapter.
- **The image proxy forwards it — but only where it belongs.** The cookie is
  passed on only for CGBUM's own hosts, so the proxy cannot be used to leak
  cookies to arbitrary sites.
- **Offline downloads send it too.** Downloading a chapter for offline reading
  now presents the same cookie and referer, so saved chapters actually contain
  images instead of error pages.
- **Covers were never affected** and still load as before.

The result: CGBUM chapter pages load normally, in the reader and in downloads.

## Notes

- The earlier v1.2.9 note blaming datacenter IP blocking has been corrected. The
  host was reachable all along; it was waiting for the cookie.
